fields.meta_description: Build a copyright release form that grants a license or transfers ownership, then files each signed release with its work. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Copyright Release Form That Names the Rights Granted
fields.hero_description: Describe the work and the rights you need. Emergent builds the copyright release form, captures the owner's signature and files each release beside its work.
fields.features_heading: What Every Copyright Release Spells Out
fields.features_subheading: A release gets read again when someone wants a use nobody discussed. These parts decide the answer in advance.
fields.feature_1:
License or transfer, chosen up front

Ask the owner whether they are granting permission to use the work or handing over ownership. The form shows the matching wording, and the choice is saved as its own field.
fields.feature_2:
The work identified exactly

Record each work's title and creation date, plus a thumbnail of it. Anyone checking a reprint months later finds the precise image or text instead of a vague description.
fields.feature_3:
Each right on its own line

List printing and editing as separate rights, plus any other use you need. The owner ticks the ones they grant and adds a term in years, and each tick is stored as its own field.
fields.feature_4:
An ownership statement from the signer

Have the signer confirm they created the work, or name whoever else holds rights in it. Any entry that names someone else is held for review before it reaches your catalog.
fields.feature_5:
Signed copies for both sides

Capture the owner's e-signature and email each party a signed PDF. The same file sits in your database next to the work, ready for the day a printer or publisher asks to see it.
fields.feature_6:
The source code is yours

Export the release app and its database to your GitHub. A developer can host it on your own servers or wire it into the gallery or submission system your team already runs.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Asks for a Copyright Release
fields.tab_content_1:
Print rights travel with every lab order

Ellis Portraits delivers a 40-image gallery to the Grant family, and Dana Grant requests a print release from the gallery page. It allows personal printing of all 40 images, while the copyright stays with the studio. When she orders prints, the lab gets the signed PDF with the order and prints without calling the studio.
fields.tab_content_2:
Catalog rights come from each artist, once

Entry to the Riverbend spring show includes a short release. Each artist lets the arts council reproduce the work in the printed catalog and on its website, and states that they own it. This year 64 artists entered. Two entries named a co-owner, and the council held both until the co-owner signed as well.
fields.tab_content_3:
The logo changes owners when the invoice is paid

Northwind Coffee hires a design studio for its new logo. The contract says the copyright in the final logo transfers on full payment. Once the $2,400 final invoice is marked paid, the designer gets the transfer to sign, and Northwind receives the signed PDF. The 3 rejected concepts stay with the studio.
fields.tab_content_4:
Ask each publisher once, then track the answer

Chapter 3 of Ana Ruiz's dissertation reuses 11 figures from published papers. She sends each publisher a permission request from one form, and every reply lands in her log with its figure. So far 9 of the 11 have granted reuse. Before the library deadline, she gets an email naming the 2 publishers that have not answered.

fields.howto_title: How to Draft a Copyright Release Form
fields.howto_description: Two decisions shape the whole document: whether ownership changes hands, and exactly which work the release covers.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Name the parties and the payment
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start by choosing between a license and a transfer of ownership. A license lets the other side use the work while the owner keeps the copyright. Under US law, a transfer of ownership is not valid unless it is in writing and signed by the owner.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Describe the work so nobody can argue about it later: the title, the file name, the creation date and a thumbnail or excerpt. For a batch of photos, add the gallery number and the image count, then attach the files themselves.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Name every right separately, such as printing or editing copies. Add how long the permission lasts and where it applies. Anything the release leaves out is a conversation for later, never an assumption either side gets to make.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Name both parties in full, the owner first, then the person or business receiving the rights. State the payment, or that there is none. When work is paid in stages, say which payment releases the rights and what happens to unused drafts.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your release wording into the prompt with the rights list and the payment rule. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it, signature step included. Change any field later by prompting, without rebuilding the form from the start.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Email both sides the signed release, and send the print lab or publisher theirs with the order. Alert one named person by email or in Slack when an entry lists a co-owner or a permission request goes unanswered.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the release as the owner: grant two rights, decline a third, then sign. Open the PDF and the database record and confirm they match line for line. Have a lawyer read the wording before the first real owner signs it.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is mostly single PDFs: an artist's release for written work and art, a sample artwork transfer, Esri's third-party permission form, Virginia Tech's thesis release, two photographers' print release pages, plus one WPForms logo template. Each gives one set of clauses for one situation and never says whether the owner is granting a license or handing over ownership, which US law treats differently. This page explains that choice, lists what every copyright release names, answers the copyright basics searchers ask about, and shows the release as an app that records each work, the rights granted and who signed.

claims_to_source: A transfer of copyright ownership is not valid unless it is in writing and signed by the owner of the rights conveyed or the owner's authorized agent

Copyright protects original works of authorship fixed in a tangible medium of expression, and does not extend to any idea, procedure, process, system, method of operation, concept, principle or discovery
Names, titles, short phrases and slogans are not protected by copyright
The copyright owner has the exclusive rights to reproduce the work, prepare derivative works, distribute copies, and perform and display it publicly
A copyright notice consists of the symbol or the word Copyright, the year of first publication and the name of the owner
A certificate of registration made before or within five years after first publication is prima facie evidence of the validity of the copyright and the facts stated in it

Statutory damages and attorney's fees are not available for infringement that begins after first publication and before registration, unless the work is registered within three months after first publication
